domicile.pt: quando um planeta está em domicílio no seu mapa, ele está no signo que ele rege (o seu trono), e tende a expressar suas qualidades de modo mais natural. é uma das dignidades do planeta.
domicile.en: when a planet is in domicile in your chart, it is in the sign it rules (its throne), and it tends to express its qualities more naturally. it is one of the planet's dignities.
reviewNotes: Structure (rules the sign, called domicile or throne, a dignity) from A12:1267-1272 and A15:45-51; the 'expresses qualities more naturally' tendency is book-only (B:17372-17377, a Moon-specific sentence generalized) because no class describes what domicile does.
Classes give no standalone definition of domicile; A15 uses it only in examples.

exaltation.pt: quando um planeta está em exaltação no seu mapa, ele está num signo onde é exaltado, e tende a ter suas qualidades favorecidas. é uma das dignidades do planeta, e o signo oposto a ele é o da queda.
exaltation.en: when a planet is in exaltation in your chart, it is in a sign where it is exalted, and it tends to have its qualities favored. it is one of the planet's dignities, and the sign opposite to it is that of its fall.
reviewNotes: Exaltation as a dignity and as the sign 180 degrees from the fall sign is from A12:1266-1272; no class says what exaltation does, so 'qualities favored' is only the reading of 'dignity' versus 'debilidade' in A12:1267-1270.
Book exaltation texts are sign-specific and partly garbled OCR; not used.

detriment.pt: quando um planeta está em detrimento (exílio) no seu mapa, ele está no signo oposto ao que rege, a 180° do seu domicílio, e tende a ter suas qualidades menos à vontade. é uma das debilidades do planeta.
detriment.en: when a planet is in detriment (exile) in your chart, it is in the sign opposite to the one it rules, 180° from its domicile, and it tends to have its qualities less at ease. it is one of the planet's debilities.
reviewNotes: Definition (ruler is always in detriment in the opposite sign, a debility) from A12:1267-1272; A15:45-47 uses exílio for the same position of the node. 'less at ease' is book-only (B:17113-17117, Sun-specific sentence generalized).
A12 and A15 use detrimento/exílio as the same status; neither describes its effect.

fall.pt: quando um planeta está em queda no seu mapa, ele está no signo oposto ao da sua exaltação, a 180° dela, e tende a ter suas qualidades desafiadas. é uma das debilidades do planeta.
fall.en: when a planet is in fall in your chart, it is in the sign opposite to that of its exaltation, 180° from it, and it tends to have its qualities challenged. it is one of the planet's debilities.
reviewNotes: Definition (exalted in the sign 180 degrees from where it falls; a debility) from A12:1266-1272; 'challenged' is book-only (B:17084-17097, Sun-specific wording generalized).
No class describes the effect of fall.

decanConcept.pt: o decanato divide cada signo em três partes de cerca de dez graus no espaço e dez dias no tempo, tradição egípcia dos trinta e seis decanatos. cada decanato é um subtom do signo: pode ajudar você a ler qualidades intrínsecas da mente, fenômenos intelectuais e emocionais e a riqueza do subconsciente. cada um é visto também como uma das trinta e seis cruzes do zodíaco.
decanConcept.en: the decan divides each sign into three parts of about ten degrees in space and ten days in time, in the Egyptian tradition of thirty-six decans. each decan is a sub-tone of the sign: it can help you read intrinsic qualities of the mind, intellectual and emotional phenomena and the richness of the subconscious. each is also seen as one of the thirty-six crosses of the zodiac.
reviewNotes: Adopted A3 104-114 (Egyptian decans: about 10 degrees/10 days, 36 counselor gods, use for intrinsic qualities of the mind and the subconscious) and A5 570-574 (36 crosses). A3 180-182 (colour of the counselor god vs sign colour) not used as it needs an unavailable colour table.

Excluded the 18 gods above and 18 below the Earth, the hemisphere (left/right) reading and the sidereal 720-year decan (A5) as not needed for a placement description; the book itself uses planetary rulers, not gods.
